_comment: Public Tableau projection. Separate from semantic/projections.json, which Cube shares. {s} is the marts schema. SQL stays portable between Snowflake and DuckDB; data_role, posting_key and the short employer id are computed in Python so both sources give the same values; every public CSV also carries that export's snapshot_kind and snapshot_id. The oracle fixes what cannot change: the LCA and OEWS values and the archived 86 job-posting rows. Daily loads add live rows, so total posting values are read from the source at export time and recorded in the manifest.

data_role.meaning: 1 when the free-text job title names data engineering, data science, data analytics, data architecture or modeling, data warehousing, ETL, analytics engineering, business intelligence or machine learning engineering. A title match only: it is not a validated occupation, and it ignores SOC. Excluded on purpose: database administrator, data center, data entry, clinical data manager.

queries.lca:
select f.case_number as case_id, f.fiscal_year, coalesce(cast(extract(year from f.received_date) as varchar)||'-'||lpad(cast(extract(month from f.received_date) as varchar),2,'0'),'UNKNOWN') as received_month,
 coalesce(f.soc_code,'UNKNOWN') as soc, coalesce(o.soc_title,'Unknown occupation') as soc_title,
 coalesce(case when g.cbsa_type='Metropolitan Statistical Area' then g.cbsa_code end,'UNKNOWN') as metro_cbsa,
 coalesce(case when g.cbsa_type='Metropolitan Statistical Area' then g.cbsa_title end,'Unknown or non-metropolitan') as metro_title,
 coalesce(f.worksite_state,'UNKNOWN') as state, case when f.is_certified then 1 else 0 end as is_certified,
 f.annual_wage, coalesce(f.employer_id,'UNKNOWN') as employer_id, f.job_title
from {s}.fact_lca_case f left join {s}.dim_occupation o using(occupation_key)
 left join {s}.dim_geography g using(geography_key)
order by f.case_number
queries.postings:
select f.posting_id, f.observation_date, case when f.is_active then 1 else 0 end as is_active,
 coalesce(f.employer_id,'UNKNOWN') as employer_id, coalesce(o.soc_code,'UNKNOWN') as soc,
 coalesce(case when g.cbsa_type='Metropolitan Statistical Area' then g.cbsa_code end,'UNKNOWN') as metro_cbsa,
 f.employer_mapping_status, f.replay_kind
from {s}.fact_job_posting_daily f left join {s}.dim_occupation o using(occupation_key)
 left join {s}.dim_geography g using(geography_key)
order by f.posting_id, f.observation_date
queries.wages:
select f.soc_code as soc, f.occupation_title as soc_title, f.area_type||':'||f.area_code as area,
 f.survey_year, f.annual_median_wage, f.annual_median_wage_raw as median_raw, f.wage_status
from {s}.fact_wage_benchmark f where f.area_type='1' order by 1,3,4
queries.benchmark:
with lca as (
 select f.soc_code as soc, g.cbsa_code as metro_cbsa, max(g.cbsa_title) as metro_title, count(*) as lca_cases,
  percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by cast(f.annual_wage as double)) as lca_p50,
  percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by cast(f.annual_wage as double)) as lca_p75,
  percentile_cont(0.9) within group (order by cast(f.annual_wage as double)) as lca_p90
 from {s}.fact_lca_case f join {s}.dim_geography g using(geography_key)
 where g.cbsa_type='Metropolitan Statistical Area' and f.soc_code is not null
 group by f.soc_code, g.cbsa_code having count(*)>={min_cases}
), ranked as (
 select l.*, row_number() over(partition by soc order by lca_cases desc, metro_cbsa) as metro_rank from lca l
), titles as (
 select soc_code, max(soc_title) as soc_title from {s}.dim_occupation group by soc_code
)
select r.soc, coalesce(t.soc_title,'Unknown occupation') as soc_title,
 r.soc||' '||coalesce(t.soc_title,'Unknown occupation') as soc_label,
 r.metro_cbsa, r.metro_title, r.lca_cases, case when r.metro_rank<={top_metros} then 1 else 0 end as metro_top25,
 r.lca_p50, r.lca_p75, r.lca_p90, w.annual_median_wage as oews_median,
 coalesce(w.wage_status,'NOT_PUBLISHED') as oews_status, {survey_year} as oews_survey_year
from ranked r left join titles t on r.soc=t.soc_code
 left join {s}.fact_wage_benchmark w on w.soc_code=r.soc and w.area_type='4'
  and w.area_code=r.metro_cbsa and w.survey_year={survey_year}
order by r.soc, r.metro_rank
queries.employer_names:
select coalesce(f.employer_id,'UNKNOWN') as employer_id, f.source_employer_name, count(*) as cases
from {s}.fact_lca_case f group by 1,2 order by 1, 3 desc, 2
queries.oracle_lca:
select count(*), count(distinct case_number), sum(case when is_certified then 1 else 0 end),
 percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by cast(annual_wage as double)) from {s}.fact_lca_case
queries.oracle_postings:
select count(*), sum(case when is_active then 1 else 0 end),
 sum(case when replay_kind='LOCAL_ARCHIVE_REPLAY' then 1 else 0 end),
 sum(case when replay_kind='LOCAL_ARCHIVE_REPLAY' and is_active then 1 else 0 end)
from {s}.fact_job_posting_daily
queries.oracle_oews:
select count(*), max(annual_median_wage) from {s}.fact_wage_benchmark
 where soc_code='15-1252' and area_type='1' and area_code='99' and survey_year=2025
queries.releases:
select 'LCA' as fact, source_release as release, count(*) as row_count from {s}.fact_lca_case group by source_release
union all select 'OEWS', source_release, count(*) from {s}.fact_wage_benchmark group by source_release
union all select 'POSTINGS', replay_kind||' '||cast(observation_date as varchar), count(*)
 from {s}.fact_job_posting_daily group by replay_kind, observation_date
order by 1,2
